November 10, 2020

  Inglewood, California
  November 10, 2020

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  November 10, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
  The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  Council Member Morales.
  City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Jacquelyn Gordon  Staff Assistant

  PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
  No. CS-1.

  *****************

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority, at the
  hour of 2:01 p.m.

  The Acting City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/ Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk /Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Jacquelyn Gordon  Staff Assistant

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. CI-1, Initiative by Council
  Member Padilla requesting approval of City Sponsorship of the 2020 Annual District 2

  1
   November 10, 2020

  Christmas Drive-thru Toy and Canned Food Drive, and O-1, Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  Salary Ordinance.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Items Nos. SPH-1, SPH-2, H-2, and O-1.

  Senator Holly Mitchell, spoke on collaborating with the Mayor and Council Members,
  and looks forward to working and meeting with the Mayor and his representatives.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/ Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded by
  Council Member/ Successor Agency Member/ Housing Authority Member Morales that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  November 6, 2020, in the amount of $4,017,323.18, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Roberto Avila for alleged personal injury; accident on July 16, 2020.
  2) Eloisa Davis- Ludlow for alleged property damage; clogged sewer on January 29,
  2020.
  3) Lisa Lundie for alleged personal injury; trip and fall on March 23, 2020.
  4) Iweka Okparaocha for alleged personal injury; illegal tow on September 6, 2020.
  5) Candace Vick for alleged vehicle damage; loose gravel on September 17, 2020.

  B. Deny the Application for Leave to Present a Late Claim Pursuant to Government
  Code, Section 911.6:
  1) Iweka Okparaocha for alleged personal injury; illegal tow on September 6, 2020.
  2) Frances & Artis Rutledge for alleged vehicle damage; pothole on December 25, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, seconded by Council Member Franklin that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject the claims listed as A1 through A5; and 2) Deny
  the application for the claims listed as B1 through B2. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21-23 ADOPTED – RATIFYING APPOINTMENT MADE TO
  THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD. Staff report dated
  November 10, 2020, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution ratifying the
  following appointment to the South Bay Workforce Investment Board: 1) On October 13,
  2020, the City of Gardena appointed Mr. Devan Metcalfe, Chief Executive Officer
  (CEO) of the Memorial Hospital of Gardena, to serve a term of office ending June 30,
  2024.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby Adopt Resolution No. 21-23 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, RATIFYING AN APPOINTMENT MADE
  TO THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD BY
  MEMBEER CITIES

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   November 10, 2020

142  COOPERATIVE BLANKET PURCHASE ORDER  APPROVED - HOME
  DEPOT. Staff report dated November 10, 2020, was presented recommending approval
  of a three-year cooperative blanket purchase order with Home Depot (with the option to
  extend three additional years in one-year increments), for the purchase of various
  maintenance, repair, and operating supplies.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve the cooperative blanket purchase order in the
  total amount of $750,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

160  PURCHASE ORDERS FOR LIBRARY SUPPLIES APPROVED - BAKER &
  TAYLOR, LLC AND BIBLIOTHECA, LLC. Staff report dated November 10, 2020,
  was presented recommending approval of a three-year annual purchase order from Baker
  & Taylor, LLC for books, cataloguing services, and library supplies, and approval of a
  three-year annual purchase order from Bibliotheca, LLC for electronic books (General
  Fund).

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve purchase order from Baker & Taylor, LLC
  in the total amount of $935,700; and 2) Approve purchase order from Bibliotheca, LLC
  in the total amount of $270, 000. The motion was carried out by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21-048 APPROVED AND PAYMENT AUTHORIZED –
  BATEMAN COMMUNITY LIVING, LLC DBA TRIO COMMUNITY MEALS;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-24 ADOPTED – AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021
  BUDGET. Staff report dated March 24, 2020, was presented recommending approval of
  an agreement with Bateman Community Living, LLC dba TRIO Community Meals to
  provide food services for the Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP).

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-048 in an amount not
  to exceed $470,000; 2) Authorize payment of invoices submitted by Bateman
  Community Living, LLC dba TRIO Community Meals for meals provided through the
  ENP in the amount not to exceed $330,000; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 21-24 entitled:
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CA AMENDING THE 2020-2021, ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  ENSURE THE FISCAL VIABILITY OF THE CITY’S SENIOR NUTRITION
  PROGRAM WHILE THE CITY REISSUES A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET - ORDINANCE AMENDING INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING), INCLUDING
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT (ZCA-2020-003), MODIFYING SELF-STORAGE
  FACILITY REGULATIONS CITYWIDE. Staff report dated November 10, 2020, was
  presented requesting that a public hearing be set to consider an ordinance amending
  Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 12 (Planning and Zoning), including Zoning Code
  Amendment (ZCA-2020-003) to modify self-storage Facility regulations citywide.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for November 24, 2020, at 2:00 p.m.

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET- AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN FOR THE MINOR HOME REPAIR PROGRAM. Staff report

  3
   November 10, 2020

  dated November 10, 2020, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider proposed substantial amendments to the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Annual Action
  Plan to reallocate program funds for the Minor Home Repair Program in the amount of
  $276, 553.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for November 17, 2020, at 2:00 p.m.

173  ORDINANCE NO. 21-01 ADOPTED – ESTABLISH SALARIES AND
  CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021. Staff report
  dated November 10, 2021, was presented recommending the adoption of Ordinance No.
  21-01 to establish salaries and conditions of employment for Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES, AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY; AND REPEALING ALL
  PREVIOUS ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT VARIANCE
  HEREWITH; THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  which was introduced at the meeting held on October 27, 2020, be adopted. The motion
  was carried out by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  ASSOCIATION (IPCMA). Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged;
  Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6; Name

  Inglewood Management Employee Organization (IMEO); Inglewood Executive
  Organization (IEO); Inglewood Police Officers Associations (IPOA); Inglewood Police
